title: Liking and disliking
about: Collocations for talking about what you like and dislike: strong noun phrases (a particular liking, the highest regard, sheer enjoyment, an intense dislike, a strong aversion), verb + noun phrases (take pride in sth, take offence, give sb a warm welcome) and ways to talk about favourites, fans and admirers.

parts.title: Other useful collocations for likes and dislikes

items.phrase: have a particular liking for sth
items.pattern: have a particular liking for sth / for doing sth · also: a special / great / strong liking
items.meaning: like one thing especially, more than others of the same kind
items.uk: особливо любити щось, мати особливу слабкість до чогось
items.example: My grandmother has a **particular liking for** dark chocolate with orange.
more: I've always had a **particular liking for** seaside towns in winter, when they're quiet.
Our cat has a **particular liking for** sleeping in the laundry basket.
items.watchOut: Після liking — for: a liking for jazz, не a liking to jazz. Але take a liking to sb — почати симпатизувати комусь. «Особлива любов» — a particular (або special) liking, не peculiar: peculiar — дивний, незвичний.

items.phrase: have a genuine liking for sb/sth
items.pattern: have a genuine / real liking for sb/sth
items.meaning: really and sincerely like someone or something, not just pretend to
items.uk: щиро любити когось / щось, мати до когось щиру симпатію
items.example: You can tell our new nurse has a **genuine liking for** old people: she always stops to chat.
more: Our son has a **genuine liking for** vegetables, which amazes our friends.
Despite all their arguments, the two brothers have a **genuine liking for** each other.
items.watchOut: Вимова: /ˈdʒenjuɪn/, у кінці «-ін», а не «-айн».

items.phrase: a great / passionate love of sth
items.pattern: a great / passionate love of (or for) sth · have / share a love of sth
items.meaning: a very strong love of an activity, a place or a subject
items.example: Her **great love of** gardening started when she helped her grandad with his roses.
more: My neighbour has a **passionate love of** the mountains and goes climbing every summer.
The two friends share a **great love of** old black-and-white films.
items.watchOut: Любов до чогось — love of або love for, не love to (калька з «до»): a love of music. «Палка любов» — passionate love, не hot love.

items.phrase: have the greatest / highest regard for sb
items.pattern: have the greatest / highest regard for sb/sth · have great regard for sb · formal
items.meaning: respect and admire someone very much
items.uk: глибоко поважати когось, ставитися до когось з величезною повагою
items.example: Everyone at the club has the **highest regard for** the woman who has coached the children's team for thirty years.
more: My dad has the **greatest regard for** the mechanic who has looked after his car for twenty years.
Teachers at the school have the **highest regard for** the caretaker, who can fix anything.
items.watchOut: Regard звучить офіційно, у розмові частіше respect. «Найбільша повага» — the highest / greatest regard, не the biggest regard. Після regard — for.

items.pattern: the sheer enjoyment of (doing) sth · for the sheer enjoyment of it · sheer = pure, complete
items.meaning: pure enjoyment, with nothing else mixed in
items.example: There's nothing like the **sheer enjoyment** of a hot bath after a long walk in the rain.
more: You could see the **sheer enjoyment** on the dog's face as he ran along the beach.
She doesn't cook to impress anyone. She does it for the **sheer enjoyment** of it.
items.watchOut: «Чисте задоволення» — sheer або pure enjoyment, не clean enjoyment: clean — чистий від бруду. Sheer підсилює й інші слова: sheer luck, sheer joy.

items.phrase: get great enjoyment out of sth
items.pattern: get (great / a lot of) enjoyment out of / from sth
items.meaning: enjoy something very much, usually again and again
items.example: My parents **get great enjoyment out of** their allotment, even when it rains.
more: The kids **got great enjoyment out of** the old tent we put up in the garden.
I **get** a lot of **enjoyment from** a long walk on Sunday mornings.
items.watchOut: «Отримувати задоволення» — get enjoyment, не receive enjoyment. Після enjoyment — out of або from: get enjoyment out of music.

items.pattern: it's / it was a great / huge pleasure to do / doing sth · such a great pleasure
items.meaning: something that is very pleasant to do or experience
items.example: Thank you for showing us round your town. It was a **great pleasure** to see it with a local.
more: After a week of camping in the rain, it was a **huge pleasure** to sleep in a real bed.
Our neighbour is moving away. It's been a **great pleasure** having her next door.
items.watchOut: «З великим задоволенням» — with great pleasure або просто with pleasure, не with big pleasure. Big з pleasure зазвичай не вживають.

items.phrase: a clear / strong preference for sth
items.pattern: have / express / show a clear / strong preference for sth (rather than / over sth else)
items.meaning: a definite feeling that you like one thing more than another
items.uk: явна / сильна перевага; явно віддавати перевагу чомусь
items.example: In the taste test, my family showed a **clear preference for** the cheaper brand of coffee.
more: My son has a **strong preference for** showers rather than baths.
Our guests usually express a **clear preference for** breakfast in the garden.
items.watchOut: Після preference — for: a preference for tea, не a preference to tea. «Явна, сильна перевага» — a clear / strong preference, не a big preference.

items.pattern: have an intense / strong / deep dislike of (or for) sth
items.meaning: a very strong feeling of not liking something
items.uk: сильна неприязнь; страшенно не любити щось
items.example: My brother has an **intense dislike of** crowded shopping centres.
more: I've had an **intense dislike of** cabbage since my school dinners.
She developed an **intense dislike of** flying after a very bumpy trip to Spain.
items.watchOut: Intense — сильний; intensive — інтенсивний (an intensive course). Тому an intense dislike, а не an intensive dislike.

items.phrase: take an instant dislike to sb/sth
items.pattern: take an instant / immediate dislike to sb/sth · take – took – taken
items.meaning: start to dislike someone or something as soon as you see or meet them
items.uk: одразу (з першого погляду) незлюбити когось / щось
items.example: My daughter **took an instant dislike to** her new piano teacher, but now they get on really well.
more: I **took an instant dislike to** the hotel: the room smelled of smoke.
Our dog **took an instant dislike to** the postman and barks at him every morning.
items.watchOut: Дієслово — take, прийменник — to: took an instant dislike to him, не made a dislike. Протилежне — take a liking to sb (почати симпатизувати).

items.phrase: a huge / strong aversion to sth
items.pattern: have a huge / strong aversion to sth / to doing sth
items.meaning: a strong feeling of dislike, or of not wanting to do something at all
items.uk: сильна відраза (огида) до чогось; страшенно не хотіти щось робити
items.example: My husband has a **strong aversion to** shopping for clothes.
more: Cats have a **huge aversion to** water, so bath time is never easy.
I've always had a **strong aversion to** horror films.
items.watchOut: Після aversion — to: an aversion to spiders, не an aversion against. Вимова: /əˈvɜːʃn/, наголос на другому складі.

items.phrase: a deep / deep-rooted hatred of sth
items.pattern: a deep hatred of (or for) sb/sth · a deep-rooted hatred (between A and B)
items.meaning: very strong hatred; deep-rooted means it has existed for a long time and is hard to change
items.example: My grandmother had a **deep hatred of** gossip and never said a bad word about anyone.
more: There's a **deep-rooted hatred** between the two neighbours that started over a garden fence forty years ago.
He has a **deep hatred of** bullying because he was bullied at school himself.
items.watchOut: Ненависть до чогось — hatred of або hatred for, не hatred to (калька з «до»). Hatred — іменник; hate — найчастіше дієслово.

items.pattern: state your preference (for sth) · formal: on forms, when you book
items.meaning: say clearly which thing you would like when you are asked to choose
items.example: When you book the cottage, you can **state your preference for** a bedroom with a sea view.
more: Patients can **state a preference** for a male or female doctor.
Please **state your preference** for a morning or afternoon appointment when you call.
items.watchOut: «Вказати, чого хочеш» в анкеті — state your preference, не tell your preference. State звучить офіційно; у розмові просто say which you'd prefer.

items.pattern: cater for sb's tastes / all tastes / everyone's tastes · cater for (UK) = cater to (US)
items.meaning: provide what different people want or like
items.uk: задовольняти всі смаки, мати щось на будь-який смак
items.example: The new market **caters for all tastes**, from cheap street food to fancy cheese.
more: Our holiday park tries to **cater for everyone's tastes**, so there's a disco and a quiet library.
It's hard to **cater for** both my parents' **tastes**: Dad loves spicy food and Mum can't stand it.
items.watchOut: Британською — cater for, американською — cater to. «На будь-який смак» — cater for all tastes; tastes тут у множині.

items.pattern: take (great / real) pride in sth / in doing sth
items.meaning: feel pleased about something you do, and do it carefully and well
items.uk: пишатися чимось (своєю роботою), вкладати в щось душу
items.example: Our local baker **takes pride in** her bread and gets up at four every morning to make it.
more: My grandad **took** great **pride in** his vegetable garden.
I **take pride in** keeping my car clean.
items.watchOut: Take pride in — з in: take pride in your work. А з прикметником — be proud of: I'm proud of my work. Не take pride of.

items.phrase: not relish the thought of (doing) sth
items.pattern: not relish the thought / prospect of (doing) sth · usually with a negative
items.meaning: not like to think about something unpleasant that is going to happen
items.uk: зовсім не тішитися думкою про щось, не хотіти навіть думати про щось
items.example: I don't **relish the thought of** driving to Scotland in the snow.
more: The kids don't **relish the thought of** going back to school after the holidays.
My sister doesn't **relish the thought of** another winter in that cold flat.
items.watchOut: Relish the thought / prospect майже завжди вживають із запереченням: I don't relish the thought of… Після of — -ing: the thought of cleaning, не the thought to clean.

items.pattern: take (great) pleasure in sth / in doing sth
items.meaning: enjoy doing something
items.uk: отримувати задоволення від чогось, із задоволенням щось робити
items.example: My aunt **takes pleasure in** baking cakes for the whole street.
more: Some people seem to **take pleasure in** other people's mistakes.
He **takes** great **pleasure in** showing visitors round his home town.
items.watchOut: Після take pleasure in — іменник або -ing: takes pleasure in cooking, не takes pleasure to cook. Не make pleasure.

items.pattern: take offence (at sth) · = be / get offended · offence (UK), offense (US)
items.meaning: become upset because you feel someone has insulted or disrespected you
items.example: I only said her soup was a bit salty, but she **took offence**.
more: Please don't **take offence at** my question. I'm just curious.
My uncle **takes offence** very easily, so don't make jokes about his football team.
items.watchOut: «Образитися» — take offence, be offended або get offended, не be offenced. Без артикля: take offence, не take an offence. Образитися на щось — take offence at sth, не on. Не take insult: an insult — це образливі слова чи дії; «сприйняти як образу» — take it as an insult.

items.pattern: have no / little sympathy for sb / for people who …
items.meaning: feel no pity for someone, usually because you think their problem is their own fault
items.example: I **have no sympathy for** drivers who ignore the 'road closed' signs and get stuck in the flood.
more: My mum **has** little **sympathy for** people who complain about the weather all the time.
I **have no sympathy for** him. He knew the shop closed at six.
items.watchOut: Sympathy — співчуття, а не «симпатія»! «Він мені симпатичний» — I like him. Sympathy for sb — співчуття до когось.

items.pattern: give sb a warm welcome · get / receive a warm welcome
items.meaning: greet someone in a very friendly way when they arrive
items.example: My cousins **gave us a warm welcome** with home-made lemonade and big hugs.
more: We always **get a warm welcome** at our favourite little café.
The whole class **gave** the new girl **a warm welcome**.
items.watchOut: «Тепло зустріти» — give sb a warm welcome, не a hot welcome. Не make a welcome.

items.pattern: sb's absolute / all-time favourite (sth) · all-time = of all time
items.meaning: the one you like best of all, more than anything else of its kind
items.example: Chocolate cake with cherries is my **absolute favourite**.
more: 'Casablanca' is my dad's **all-time favourite** film.
Of all the places we've been on holiday, Crete is our **all-time favourite**.
items.watchOut: «Найулюбленіший» — my absolute / all-time favourite. My most favourite у розмові інколи чути, але зазвичай це вважають помилкою: favourite уже означає «найбільш улюблений». Британське написання — favourite.

items.pattern: a great / real / true lover of sth · a music / nature / animal lover
items.meaning: someone who likes something very much
items.example: My grandmother was a **great lover of** poetry and could recite whole poems by heart.
more: As a **great lover of** dogs, he stops to stroke every one he meets in the park.
I'm not a **great lover of** big parties. I prefer dinner with a few friends.
items.watchOut: Lover of + що саме: a lover of nature, a music lover. Без цього (my lover) lover означає «коханий / коханка», тож будь обережний.

items.phrase: an ardent / dedicated fan of sth
items.pattern: an ardent / dedicated / big fan of sb/sth
items.meaning: someone who likes or supports a team, a singer, a kind of music, etc. with strong feelings
items.example: My neighbour is an **ardent fan of** country music and goes to Nashville every few years.
more: She's a **dedicated fan of** the band and has seen them live twelve times.
Our teacher is an **ardent fan of** crime novels.
items.watchOut: «Палкий шанувальник» — an ardent fan, не a hot fan. Ardent вимовляється /ˈɑːdnt/. Після fan — of: a fan of jazz.

items.pattern: a keen / great admirer of sb/sth
items.meaning: someone who admires a person or their work very much
items.example: My mother is a **keen admirer of** Van Gogh and has a print of his sunflowers in the kitchen.
more: I'm a **keen admirer of** people who can stay calm in a crisis.
Our son is a **keen admirer of** the firefighters at the local station and waves every time their engine goes past.
items.watchOut: Keen тут — «палкий, завзятий» (a keen gardener — завзятий садівник). Admirer — людина (шанувальник), admiration — почуття (захоплення).

items.pattern: sb/sth fills sb with admiration · be filled with admiration (for sb) · be full of admiration for sb
items.meaning: make someone admire a person or what they have done very much
items.uk: викликати в когось захоплення, сповнювати захопленням
items.example: The way the nurses worked through the night **filled me with admiration**.
more: My little sister's courage at the hospital **filled us all with admiration**.
I **was filled with admiration** for the volunteers who cleaned the beach after the storm.
items.watchOut: Fill sb with admiration — з with, не of. Але з прикметником full — of: I'm full of admiration for her.

items.pattern: it gives sb (great) pleasure to do sth / when … · sth gives sb pleasure
items.meaning: make someone feel happy and pleased
items.example: It **gives me pleasure** to watch the birds in the garden every morning.
more: Gardening **gives** my dad more **pleasure** than anything else.
It **gives** her great **pleasure** when the neighbours' kids wave to her from their window.
items.watchOut: «Приносити задоволення» — give sb pleasure, не make sb pleasure. «Мені приємно» — it gives me pleasure або I'm pleased.

warmup.uk: Діти верещали від щирого задоволення, катаючись на гірці.
warmup.q: The kids were screaming with ___ enjoyment on the slide.
warmup.explain: Чисте, щире задоволення — sheer (або pure) enjoyment. Clean — чистий від бруду, sharp — гострий.

warmup.uk: Було дуже приємно з вами працювати.
warmup.q: It's been a ___ pleasure working with you.
warmup.explain: Велике задоволення — a great (або huge) pleasure. A big pleasure — калька з «велике задоволення», так не кажуть; так само with great pleasure, не with big pleasure.

warmup.uk: Моя сестра страшенно не любить галасливих вечірок.
warmup.q: My sister has an ___ dislike of noisy parties.
warmup.explain: Сильна неприязнь — an intense dislike. Intensive — інтенсивний (an intensive course), intent — зосереджений.

warmup.uk: Наш кіт одразу незлюбив нового пса.
warmup.q: Our cat ___ an instant dislike to the new dog.
warmup.explain: Одразу незлюбити — take an instant dislike to sb/sth.
Образитися на щось — take offence at sth. On тут — калька з «на».

warmup.q: The hotel owners gave us a ___ welcome.
warmup.explain: Тепло зустріти — give sb a warm welcome. Hot welcome не кажуть, а heated — «розпалений, гарячий» (a heated argument).

warmup.q: Ice cream is my ___ favourite dessert.
warmup.explain: Найулюбленіший — my absolute (або all-time) favourite. My most favourite у розмові буває, але зазвичай це вважають помилкою.

warmup.uk: Ця робота приносить мені багато радості.
warmup.q: This job ___ me a lot of pleasure.
warmup.explain: Приносити задоволення — give sb pleasure. Make sb pleasure — калька.

A.q: The whole village has the highest ___ for the couple who run the post office.
A.explain: Глибоко поважати — have the highest regard for sb. Admirer — людина, pleasure — задоволення.

A.q: Our dog has a huge aversion ___ the vacuum cleaner and hides under the bed.
A.explain: Після aversion — to: an aversion to sth.

A.q: She has a deep hatred ___ lies, so always tell her the truth.
A.explain: Ненависть до чогось — hatred of (або for), не to.

B.q: She ___ no sympathy for her brother: he spent all his holiday money on the first day.
B.explain: Have no sympathy for sb — зовсім не співчувати. Sympathy — співчуття, а не симпатія.

B.q: The new food court tries to ___ for everyone's tastes.
B.explain: Cater for all tastes — мати щось на будь-який смак.

B.q: I don't ___ the thought of telling Mum I've broken her favourite vase.
B.explain: Not relish the thought of sth — зовсім не тішитися думкою про щось.

C.q: My grandad learned to swim at seventy, and that filled us ___ admiration.
C.explain: Fill sb with admiration. Але: be full of admiration.

C.q: My dentist is a great ___ of classical music and plays it during every appointment.
C.explain: A great lover of sth — великий любитель (людина). A great love of sth — велика любов (почуття).

C.q: I've seen 'Up' twenty times. It's my ___ favourite film.
C.explain: Найулюбленіший за всі часи — all-time favourite, без -s.

example.title: Meeting his parents
example.uk:
Минулого літа я вперше познайомилася з батьками свого хлопця. Мене зовсім не тішила думка про цілі вихідні з незнайомими людьми, але вони тепло мене зустріли. Його мама дуже пишається своїм садом, і коли вона показувала мені свої троянди, я бачила на її обличчі щиру насолоду.

Його тато — палкий уболівальник крикету, і всю вечерю говорив про нього. Чесно кажучи, спортивні трансляції викликають у мене сильну відразу, але я не хотіла, щоб він образився, тож ставила багато запитань.

До неділі я вже глибоко поважала їх обох. Було дуже приємно провести з ними вихідні, а яблучний пиріг його мами тепер мій найулюбленіший.
example.en:
Last summer I met my boyfriend's parents for the first time. I didn't [[relish the thought|b4]] of a whole weekend with people I didn't know, but they [[gave me a warm welcome|b8]]. His mum [[takes great pride in|b3]] her garden, and I could see the [[sheer enjoyment|a5]] on her face as she showed me her roses.

His dad is an [[ardent fan|c3]] of cricket and talked about it all through dinner. To be honest, I have a [[strong aversion to|a11]] sport on TV, but I didn't want him to [[take offence|b6]], so I asked lots of questions.

By Sunday I had the [[greatest regard for|a4]] them both. It was [[a great pleasure|a7]] to spend the weekend with them, and his mum's apple pie is now my [[all-time favourite|c1]].
